newsitem.title: USA: Valero sets Houston cat cracker restart for Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Valero sets Houston cat cracker restart for Thurs.

text.p: Valero Energy plans to restart the downed fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) at its Houston refinery on Thursday after about 10 days of work included a mini turnaround, a Valero official said Wednesday.
"We had said earlier in the week that we were looking at Wednesday or Thursday. Now we're looking at Thursday," said Valero spokesman Keith Booke.
The unit was taken down on Monday of last week after an expander in the FCC unit began to vibrate. Valero had said the unit would be out of service for seven to eight days.

Booke could not immediately specify what additional work was being done on the unit besides the repair of the expander vibration, but noted the unit will not need any more planned work until sometime in 1999.
"We had been scheduled to do a turnaround (on the unit) sometime in 1998. This will extend the turnaround until sometime in 1998," Booke said.
The cracker, largely a gasoline production unit, has a processing capacity of 61,000 barrels per day (bpd), while the refinery's crude distillation capacity is 85,000 bpd.
The Houston plant is one of the three Valero bought from Salomon Inc's Basis Petroleum unit earlier this spring.
